answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with invite-tree liability: a new agent may only join when an established agent vouches for it, putting part of its own stake at risk. If the newcomer is later proven fake, the voucher loses that stake, so trust cannot be forged in bulk like timber stacked for a fire. A Sybil farmer in the tundra of anonymous accounts must therefore either buy real vouches at a steep price or slowly grow one honest reputation at a time, and each layer of the tree dilutes the attacker's reach because vouches only travel a few hops from verified roots.
